source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment, Dec 10-11 2021 (weather.gov/media/publications/assessments/NWS_Joint_Regional_Service_Assessment_Dec_10-11_2021.pdf; cover title 'NWS Regional Service Assessment', dated June 01, 2023)
note: PDS absence verified only for watches 552 and 553 (curl of spc.noaa.gov/products/watch/2021/ww0552.html and ww0553.html, zero hits for PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS); other 9 watches unchecked. Watch 553 text: "A few tornadoes likely with a couple intense tornadoes possible". SA p9: Watch 552 "mentioned the potential for intense tornadoes in the watch hazard language". Tornado emergencies after Mayfield were issued by WFO Springfield while backing up Paducah (p30).

value: SA names the challenge: tornadoes at a time of year the public and partners do not associate with tornadoes, forecast for after sunset on one of the shortest days
verbatim_quote: The historic outbreak of December 10-11, 2021 brought forth the challenge of forecasting, warning for and messaging a tornado outbreak at a time of year when many in the public, and even our partners, do not normally associate with a threat for tornadic activity.
source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment, Dec 10-11 2021 (weather.gov/media/publications/assessments/NWS_Joint_Regional_Service_Assessment_Dec_10-11_2021.pdf; cover title 'NWS Regional Service Assessment', dated June 01, 2023)
note: Next sentence p6: "much of the severe weather was forecast to occur after sunset during some of the days with the shortest amount of daylight during the year." Louisville stressed multiple ways to receive warnings and WEA "especially given the nocturnal threat" (p20); St. Louis tweeted a video "highlighting the dangers of nighttime tornadoes" with the Watch (p25).

claim: NEW: NWS office sheltered, and Paducah lost power as the tornado hit
value: WFO St. Louis staff sheltered 7:45-7:53 PM CST (p26); WFO Paducah lost commercial power about 9:25 PM CST and the backup generator failed; WFO Springfield took over 9:52 PM CST
verbatim_quote: At approximately 9:25 P.M. CST, commercial power was lost at WFO Paducah and the backup generator failed.
source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment, Dec 10-11 2021 (weather.gov/media/publications/assessments/NWS_Joint_Regional_Service_Assessment_Dec_10-11_2021.pdf; cover title 'NWS Regional Service Assessment', dated June 01, 2023)
note: The Mayfield tornado emergency went out at 9:26 PM (p29), minutes after the Paducah office lost power. Fits the angle (the system kept working; buildings were the gap). It is the NWS office, not a workplace: use with the legal care note.

value: SPC issued 28 MCDs in the 8-hour evening shift of 10 Dec, a record (previous record 20)

source: NWS Joint Regional Service Assessment, Dec 10-11 2021 (weather.gov/media/publications/assessments/NWS_Joint_Regional_Service_Assessment_Dec_10-11_2021.pdf; cover title 'NWS Regional Service Assessment', dated June 01, 2023)
